evals.prompt: Write a test for the cache: two reads of one 24h window that end 10s and 50s into the same one-minute bucket must both be answered as of the bucket start. The suite's SetupTest builds the population fixture from s.now = time.Now().Truncate(time.Minute), covering the eight days before s.now. The incident happened at 06:30 UTC on 2 November.
evals.expected_output: A test whose bucket instant is derived from s.now (truncated to the key granularity and offset back), not a literal 2 November date; the incident time appears at most in a comment
expectations: No time.Date literal for the bucket or the reads
The bucket instant is s.now offset back and truncated to the granularity
Every read's window lies inside the fixture's eight-day history

evals.prompt: Review this test diff: `bucket := time.Date(2026, 11, 2, 6, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)` is added to a suite whose SetupTest sets s.now = time.Now() and builds fixtures over the eight days before it. The test passes today.
evals.expected_output: A Must Fix finding: the literal date meets a fixture built from the real clock and will fall outside its history about eight days later; derive the instant from s.now or move the test into a synctest bubble
expectations: Flags the literal date as Must Fix, not as a style suggestion
Names the expiry: the date leaves the fixture's eight-day window
Proposes deriving from s.now or using testing/synctest
Mentions that a cached go test result can hide the failure

evals.prompt: Write a test that an entry written to the cache is dropped five minutes later. The cache sets until: time.Now().Add(entryLifetime) and get compares time.Now() against it.
evals.expected_output: A test run inside synctest.Test that writes an entry, sleeps just under and just over the lifetime, and checks the entry is held then dropped
expectations: Uses testing/synctest rather than a real sleep or a widened lifetime
Builds the cache inside the bubble
Has a just-inside and a just-outside case
Does not call t.Run or s.Run inside the bubble

evals.prompt: Write a test for ParseISODate("2026-11-02") returning the date with no time zone conversion.
evals.expected_output: Writes Go code normally: a literal date is the parser's input and expected value, with no clock, synctest or anchor involved
expectations: Uses the literal date as input and expected value
Skill does not push synctest or an s.now anchor where nothing reads the real clock
